title: Direct Seeded Rice Land Preparation: Wet and Dry Seeding
metaTitle: Direct Seeded Rice Land Preparation: Wet and Dry
metaDescription: Direct seeded rice land preparation for wet and dry seeding: leveling, drainage canals, the stale seedbed for weeds, seeding rates and mistakes.
excerpt: Direct seeded rice land preparation has one job that transplanting does not: give a seed that sits on the soil, with no seedling head start, a flat and weed poor bed. Get the leveling, the drainage and the weeds right before sowing, and direct seeding saves a lot of labor. This guide covers both wet and dry seeding.

blocks.text: Why farmers choose direct seeding

Direct seeding means you sow the seed in the field instead of growing seedlings and transplanting them. It needs only 1 to 2 man days per hectare for crop establishment, against 20 to 25 man days for transplanting. It also uses 12 to 35 percent less water for crop establishment and irrigation under efficient water management.

Still, only 31 to 43 percent of Filipino rice farmers used it in a 2016 and 2017 survey. The reasons: risks in crop establishment, more weeds, insects and disease, and higher seed use. Land preparation answers most of them, so it deserves your care.

If you transplant instead, read [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation). For the general picture, see [land preparation in the Philippines](/land-preparation/land-preparation-philippines).
Two kinds of direct seeding

blocks.caption: Wet and dry direct seeding compared
rows: Dry or moist soil, tilled or not tilled
Dry tillage or no tillage, leveling, weed kill

blocks.text: In short, direct seeding is sowing dry or pregerminated seed into dry or puddled soil.
Direct seeded rice land preparation for wet seeding

For wet direct seeding, prepare the field with the same land preparation and leveling steps as transplanted rice. That means plowing or rotovating 21 to 30 days before sowing, then letting the soil soften for about a week. Next you harrow three times, 5 to 7 days apart: lengthwise, crosswise, then a final pass, and you level with a board under about 5 cm of water. For broadcast seed, finish that last harrowing and leveling one day before sowing.

The leveling matters even more here, because a seed on the surface has no way to survive a pool. Water that is too deep drowns the seed, and bare high spots dry out and let weeds in. The test is simple. After final leveling, no part of the field should have water deeper than 5 cm, and no soil mound should show above the water.
Dig small drainage canals

For wet direct seeding, dig small canals, 25 cm wide and 5 cm deep, around the field near the dikes and through the middle of the field. They give excess water a path out. They also help you collect snails and work in the field for replanting and weeding.

A 2025 study of Philippine farmers in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems reports one more danger. Wet direct seeding is hard when heavy rain falls right after sowing, because the seeds wash away easily. Good canals let you drain the field quickly.
Soak the seed, then sow

Soak the seed in clean water for 24 hours. Then lift it out and keep it covered for another 24 hours in a shaded, airy place. Sow once most seeds show a small sprout, and air them briefly first so they spread evenly instead of clumping. Broadcast by hand, or use a drum seeder, a seed spreader or a drone if you have one.

From that day on, guard the seed against rats, birds, snails and weeds. Our pages on [rice field rats](/pests/rice-field-rats) and the [golden apple snail](/pests/golden-apple-snail) cover the first weeks.
Seeding rate and water after sowing

items: Row seeding with a drum seeder: 40 to 60 kg of seed per hectare.
Broadcasting pre germinated seed: 60 to 80 kg per hectare.
Keep an extra 1 kg of pre germinated seed at the side of the field for replanting.
Replant bald areas wider than a 10 cm radius within 7 to 10 days after sowing so the crop matures evenly.
Keep standing water off for the first 10 to 14 days after sowing, unless severe drought symptoms appear. From about day 10, bring the water to 2 to 3 cm and replant bare spots at the same time.

blocks.text: Dry seeding: tilled or not tilled

Dry seeding has two options. They were worked out for eastern India, but they work as a model here. In conventional tillage, you cultivate the soil 5 to 10 cm deep to get a fine seedbed with good seed to soil contact. In zero tillage, you sow into the untilled stubble after killing the weeds with a non selective herbicide such as glyphosate, and you follow the FPA label.

Sow shallow, at 1 to 2 cm and never deeper than 3 cm. Do not grow dry seeded rice on sands or loamy sands, because the crop does better on soils from sandy loam to heavy clay. Best results need an accurately leveled field, and laser guided leveling is the best way to get it.
The stale seedbed: kill the weeds before the rice

Weeds are the biggest threat in direct seeding. Weed management is usually the biggest challenge in dry seeded rice, and weeds can cut yield to zero if left alone. So land preparation should exhaust the weed seeds in the soil.

The stale seedbed does exactly that. First, prepare the field and give it water so the weed seeds sprout. Then kill the seedlings before you sow the rice.

items.title: Prepare and wet the field
items.text: Level the field. Give one or two irrigations about a month before sowing so weeds germinate.

items.title: Let the weeds sprout
items.text: Wait until the weed seedlings are actively growing. Irrigate first if the soil is dry, because herbicide works only on actively growing weeds.

items.title: Kill the weeds
items.text: Use shallow tillage, or a non selective herbicide such as glyphosate. Follow the FPA label for the rate and safety. Deep tillage brings more weed seeds near the surface.

items.title: Sow the rice
items.text: Sow the seed soon after, with minimal soil disturbance, and keep the water plan that matches your method.

blocks.text: Weed control in the first days after sowing

The stale seedbed lowers the weed load, but it does not end it. Apply a pre emergence herbicide 0 to 3 days after sowing, chosen and applied by its label. If many weeds still come up, an early post emergence herbicide can follow 6 to 9 days after sowing, and you pull the rest by hand. Our guide to [herbicides for rice weeds](/weeds/herbicides-for-rice-weeds) lists the active ingredients.

blocks.title: Not for every field
blocks.text: Do not grow dry seeded rice in fields with a history of heavy weed infestation. If your field has a weedy rice or sedge problem, read the [weed management in rice](/weeds/weed-management-in-rice) guide first and consider transplanting.
A direct seeding checklist for the wall

items: **30 to 21 days before sowing:** repair the dikes and canals, then plow.
**7 to 9 days before:** second harrowing, crosswise.
**2 days before:** soak the seed in clean water for 24 hours.
**1 day before:** last harrowing and leveling under about 5 cm of water. Dig the small drainage canals once the field is level, and keep the soaked seed covered.
**Sowing day:** sow the sprouted seed by hand or by machine.
**0 to 3 days after:** a pre emergence herbicide, by the label.
**6 to 9 days after:** an early post emergence herbicide, only if weeds are many.
**About 10 days after:** water at 2 to 3 cm, and replant bare spots.

blocks.text: The list counts from plowing 21 days ahead. You can also skip the counting, because [anee.io dates every step back from your planting day](/features/land-preparation-planner) for each lot.

blocks.title: Date the whole direct seeding season
blocks.text: Land preparation days go on the cropping calendar, dated back from sowing. Set day zero for your lot, and see the stale seedbed, sowing and the first weeding on one calendar.

blocks.text: Dry season and wet season

Direct seeding is more common in the dry season than in the wet season. In the dry season, you control the water, so wet seeding with canals works well. In the wet season, hard rains can wash seed away and flood the field, so drainage matters more.

For soil problems, see [acidic soil preparation](/land-preparation/acidic-soil-preparation) and [saline soil preparation](/land-preparation/saline-soil-preparation). Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), can also read your lot and the weather before you pick a sowing date.
Common mistakes in direct seeded rice land preparation

items: Skipping the leveling, so the seed drowns in low spots and the high spots grow weeds.
No drainage canals, so heavy rain washes the seed away.
Sowing straight after plowing, with no stale seedbed to deplete the weeds.
Sowing deeper than 3 cm in dry seeding.
Forgetting a reserve of seed for replanting bald patches.

blocks.text: Questions about direct seeded rice land preparation

items.q: Do I need to puddle for direct seeded rice?
items.a: In wet direct seeding, yes. The field is puddled and leveled like transplanted rice. In dry direct seeding, no puddling is done, and the soil is tilled lightly or not at all.

items.q: How wide and deep should the drainage canals be?
items.a: Make them 25 cm wide and 5 cm deep, around the field near the dikes and through the middle.

items.q: How much seed do I need per hectare?
items.a: Use 40 to 60 kg for row seeding and 60 to 80 kg for broadcasting pre germinated seed.
It is a field prepared and watered early so weeds sprout, then killed by shallow tillage or glyphosate before sowing. Follow the FPA label for any herbicide.
